keyPoints.en: First line: physical and chemical barriers — skin, mucous membranes, cilia, stomach acid, lysozyme in tears and saliva.
keyPoints.bm: Barisan pertama: penghalang fizikal dan kimia — kulit, membran mukus, silia, asid perut, lisozim dalam air mata dan air liur.

keyPoints.en: Second line (non-specific): phagocytes (neutrophils, monocytes/macrophages) engulf pathogens; inflammation and fever.
keyPoints.bm: Barisan kedua (tidak spesifik): fagosit (neutrofil, monosit/makrofaj) menelan patogen; keradangan dan demam.

keyPoints.en: Third line (specific): lymphocytes recognise specific antigens and produce antibodies and memory cells.
keyPoints.bm: Barisan ketiga (spesifik): limfosit mengecam antigen tertentu dan menghasilkan antibodi serta sel ingatan.

keyPoints.en: Inflammation: injured area becomes red, warm and swollen as more blood and phagocytes arrive.
keyPoints.bm: Keradangan: kawasan cedera menjadi merah, panas dan bengkak apabila lebih banyak darah dan fagosit tiba.

question.en: Why does a cut increase the risk of infection?

answer.en: It breaks the skin, the first line of defence, letting pathogens enter.
answer.bm: Ia memecahkan kulit, barisan pertahanan pertama, membolehkan patogen masuk.

tip.en: Non-specific = attacks any invader. Specific = targets one particular antigen.
tip.bm: Tidak spesifik = menyerang mana-mana penceroboh. Spesifik = menyasar satu antigen tertentu.

keyPoints.en: Antigens are foreign molecules (often proteins) on pathogens or toxins.
keyPoints.bm: Antigen ialah molekul asing (selalunya protein) pada patogen atau toksin.

keyPoints.en: B-lymphocytes produce Y-shaped antibodies with binding sites that match one antigen.
keyPoints.bm: Limfosit B menghasilkan antibodi berbentuk Y dengan tapak pengikatan yang sepadan dengan satu antigen.

keyPoints.en: Actions: neutralisation (block toxins), agglutination (clump), lysis (burst cells), opsonisation (mark for phagocytes).
keyPoints.bm: Tindakan: peneutralan (sekat toksin), aglutinasi (gumpal), lisis (pecahkan sel), opsonisasi (tanda untuk fagosit).

keyPoints.en: Memory cells remain after infection, giving a faster response next time.
keyPoints.bm: Sel ingatan kekal selepas jangkitan, memberi gerak balas lebih cepat pada masa akan datang.

question.en: Why does an antibody for measles not protect against chickenpox?
question.bm: Mengapa antibodi campak tidak melindungi daripada cacar air?

answer.en: Antibodies are specific; the chickenpox antigen has a different shape.
answer.bm: Antibodi adalah spesifik; antigen cacar air mempunyai bentuk berbeza.

tip.en: Draw an antibody: two heavy + two light chains, with binding sites at the tips of the Y.
tip.bm: Lukis antibodi: dua rantai berat + dua rantai ringan, dengan tapak pengikatan di hujung Y.

keyPoints.en: Active immunity: your body makes its own antibodies and memory cells — slower to develop but long-lasting.
keyPoints.bm: Keimunan aktif: badan menghasilkan antibodi dan sel ingatan sendiri — lambat terbentuk tetapi tahan lama.

keyPoints.en: Natural active: after an infection. Artificial active: vaccination.
keyPoints.bm: Aktif semula jadi: selepas jangkitan. Aktif buatan: pemvaksinan.

keyPoints.en: Passive immunity: ready-made antibodies received — immediate but short-term (no memory cells).
keyPoints.bm: Keimunan pasif: antibodi sedia ada diterima — serta-merta tetapi jangka pendek (tiada sel ingatan).

keyPoints.en: Natural passive: through the placenta and breast milk. Artificial passive: antiserum (anti-venom, anti-tetanus).
keyPoints.bm: Pasif semula jadi: melalui plasenta dan susu ibu. Pasif buatan: antiserum (antibisa, anti-tetanus).

keyPoints.en: Booster doses raise antibody levels above the immunity level for longer.
keyPoints.bm: Dos penggalak menaikkan aras antibodi melebihi aras keimunan untuk tempoh lebih lama.

question.bm: Mengapa ibu perlu menyusukan bayi yang baru lahir?

answer.en: Colostrum contains antibodies that give the baby natural passive immunity.
answer.bm: Kolostrum mengandungi antibodi yang memberi bayi keimunan pasif semula jadi.

tip.en: Two questions: who makes the antibodies (active/passive)? How did they get them (natural/artificial)?
tip.bm: Dua soalan: siapa menghasilkan antibodi (aktif/pasif)? Bagaimana diperoleh (semula jadi/buatan)?

keyPoints.en: AIDS: HIV destroys T-helper lymphocytes, weakening immunity; spread through blood, unprotected sex, sharing needles and from mother to baby.
keyPoints.bm: AIDS: HIV memusnahkan limfosit T-pembantu, melemahkan keimunan; tersebar melalui darah, seks tanpa perlindungan, berkongsi jarum dan dari ibu kepada bayi.

keyPoints.en: Allergy: immune system overreacts to harmless substances (dust mites, pollen, seafood) — sneezing, rash, asthma.
keyPoints.bm: Alahan: sistem imun bertindak berlebihan terhadap bahan tidak berbahaya (hama habuk, debunga, makanan laut) — bersin, ruam, asma.

keyPoints.en: Autoimmune diseases: immune system attacks the body's own cells (lupus/SLE, type 1 diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis).
keyPoints.bm: Penyakit autoimun: sistem imun menyerang sel badan sendiri (lupus/SLE, diabetes jenis 1, artritis reumatoid).

keyPoints.en: Organ transplants can be rejected; patients take immunosuppressant drugs.
keyPoints.bm: Pemindahan organ boleh ditolak; pesakit mengambil ubat imunosupresan.

question.en: Why do AIDS patients often die from simple infections like pneumonia?
question.bm: Mengapa pesakit AIDS sering mati akibat jangkitan biasa seperti pneumonia?

answer.en: With few T-helper cells, the body can't mount an immune response, so pathogens multiply freely.
answer.bm: Dengan sedikit sel T-pembantu, badan tidak dapat menghasilkan gerak balas imun, jadi patogen membiak dengan bebas.

tip.en: Immunodeficiency = too WEAK. Allergy/autoimmunity = too STRONG or misdirected.
tip.bm: Imunodefisiensi = terlalu LEMAH. Alahan/autoimun = terlalu KUAT atau tersasar.
